responses.message: why is everyone on my timeline posting about the strait of malacca

Two things collided overnight:

1. A large container ship lost power near the Singapore end of the strait, and traffic slowed for several hours while tugs moved it. Footage of the queue went viral.
2. A few big geopolitics accounts used it to re-up the "Malacca dilemma" — the idea that a huge share of China's oil imports pass through one narrow chokepoint that the US Navy could in theory close.

The ship's been moved and traffic is normal. The dilemma posts are mostly recycled takes.

responses.message: how real is the malacca dilemma in 2026 tho

Still real, less acute than it was. China has added pipelines (Myanmar, Central Asia, Russia), strategic petroleum reserves, and more overland supply, and there are alternate straits (Lombok, Sunda) at a cost in time. A blockade would hurt, but it's not the single off-switch it's sometimes posted as.
